newsitem.title: UK: BARCLAYS URGED BY UNION TO RESUME PAY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: BARCLAYS URGED BY UNION TO RESUME PAY TALKS.

text.p: One of the unions representing British banking and finance workers said on Thursday it was urging Barclays Bank to resume pay negotiations after talks to avert a dispute broke down earlier this week.

"The (Barclays) directors and shareholders can expect to do well out of the profits announced today but over half of the staff...will receive no increase in salary for the foreseeable future," Banking Insurance and Finance Union (BIFU) negotiating officer Jennifer Cole said in a statement.
Barclays is due to announce first-half profits later on Thursday, with financial analysts expecting pre-tax profits of 1.256 billion pounds.

A spokeswoman for Barclays told Reuters it was prepared to talk to the unions but would not re-open negotiations in a dispute linked to performance-linked pay, which will affect some 60,000 members of staff.

"We spent five months with the unions negotiating the pay deal, during which time we made significant changes (to the deal). Any further changes would compromise the principle of performance-related pay," she said.
Staff at the bank are due to start an overtime ban within the next two weeks in protest at the pay proposals, which the union says, will impose a pay freeze on 25,000 staff.

The date for the start of the overtime ban would be set next week, BIFU said. The unions expected the overtime ban to severely disrupt business and delay customer accounts and transactions. Cash machines were also likely to be affected.
Barclays said it expected the impact of the industrial action to be "minimal".
BIFU is co-ordinating the dispute with another union UNiFI. UNiFI said on Monday it would go ahead with industrial action after the bank broke off talks with it and BIFU.
Talks broke down after just two days, when the bank refused to refer a pay-and-grading structure dispute to the government industrial relations arbitration service ACAS.
BIFU, which represents several thousand employees in the bank, had earlier voted for strike action.
